As a musician, teacher and song leader, Roy's goal is to guide singers of all levels past self-judgment and fear to help them connect with their inner music. He's studied extensively with Bobby McFerrin, Rhiannon, Judi Vinar, as well as Meredith Monk, Siobhan Robinsong, and many others.

events.title: All Seasons Intergenerational Choir Fall Session*
events.description: Explore the joy of singing with others in the All Seasons Choir, an intergenerational community choir designed to bring people of many generations together in a fun and welcoming environment. All experience and skill levels are welcome, and no audition is required! Although participants can expect to pick up some new skills, the emphasis of this choir is on connecting and having fun as we sing rather than learning the nuts and bolts of music theory. We will rehearse a collection of songs on Monday evenings in August through November and culminate with an end-of-season performance. Exact dates are: 8/24, 8/31, (9/7 Labor Day, no rehearsal), 9/14, 9/21, 9/28, 10/5, (10/12 no rehearsal), 10/19, 10/26, 11/2, 11/9, 11/16, 11/23, 11/30. Click here to view the application (Application will open July 1st) Email scrain@denverlibrary.org with questions. About the instructor, Tyler Wigginton is a Denver-based composer, arranger, and performer with a degree in Music Composition from Metropolitan State University of Denver, where he earned multiple honors including the ISAM 2nd Place Composition Award and the Max DiJulio Prize. He is a certified Musicality Judge with the Barbershop Harmony Society and a three-time Rocky Mountain District quartet champion, currently singing bass in the international top-ten quartet Sunday Night Social. Tyler also serves as music director of the internationally ranked Sound of the Rockies, leading the chorus to a 5th-place international finish and a medal in 2025. An in-demand coach and educator, he teaches nationally while balancing life with tabletop RPGs, rock climbing, reading, and time with his family.

events.title: Memory Cafe: Create with Purple Art
events.description: Theme: Create with Purple Art Description: During this program, participants will maneuver small squares and rectangles of colorful recycled paintings to create beautiful paper mosaics. About Presenters: Purple Art provides innovative, expressive art programming for older adults at all levels of care at libraries, day programs and residential communities along the Front Range. We believe that creative activity is crucial to growing and healing and that everyone can access their creative selves and have fun in the process. Abby Sivy and Cindy Parker have owned and run Purple Art and Bohemia, a community studio in North Boulder, for almost 10 years. Our beliefs and teaching methods inspire introspection and expression and allow participants to articulate the richness of life experiences, spark imagination and conversation, release inhibitions and forge human connection. Abby attended Parsons School of Design and has been teaching art for decades to people of all ages. Cindy has worked with older adults since 2010 and teaches art to adults of all ages while maintaining a busy studio practice of her own. This program is designed specifically for individuals with memory loss or dementia and their care partner or family members. Attendance by groups is not part of our program model. If you are a service provider and would like to bring 3 or more people, please email olderadults@denverlibrary.org at least 2 business days before the program and we will let you know if we are able accommodate your group.

Please plan to arrive early, tours start promptly at the given time and late arrivals cannot be accommodated. events.title: Silent Pages Society: Nocturne
events.description: This night belongs to the readers. On December 7, the Society takes over Catbird Hotel. For one night, the hotel becomes an after-dark hideaway for readers. Settle into the lobby, find a corner at The Rook bar, or curl up beside the firepits on the outdoor rooftop deck. There's seating throughout, but for those who want to make a little world of their own, an enormous heated rooftop tent awaits, filled with atmospheric projections and the live ambient sounds of Field Theory. The tent is yours to make cozy. Bring blankets, pillows, or a folding chair and settle in. There's even a bar inside. Downstairs, composer Nathan Hall and musician Ryan Fiegl create an atmospheric soundscape, while ambient and environmental projections and digital art by Richard Mapes bring another dimension to the evening. Follow the music. Find your corner. Order a drink. Open your book. Silent Pages Society is a roaming literary gathering that transforms unexpected places across Denver into sanctuaries for the written word. A special thank you to our creative partners at Catbird Hotel for joining Denver Public Library in bringing this evening to life. Introverts welcome. Conversations optional. Connections possible. Event Details Date: Monday, December 7, 2026 Time: Check-in begins at 6:30 PM | Event ends at 9:30 PM Location: Catbird Hotel | 3770 Walnut St, Denver, CO 80205 Check-In: Enter through Catbird Hotel's corner entrance at 38th St. & Walnut St. in Denver's RiNo Art District. Private Event: The hotel's first floor and entire top floor are reserved exclusively for registered Silent Pages Society guests. This event is not open to the general public without registration. Make Yourself Comfortable: Seating is available throughout the hotel, including the lobby, The Rook bar, and outdoor rooftop deck. The extra-large heated rooftop tent is an open space, so guests are encouraged to bring blankets, pillows, or folding chairs to create their own cozy reading spots. Live Ambient Music: Nathan Hall & Ryan Fiegl — First floor Field Theory — Heated rooftop tent Visual Art: Ambient and environmental projections and digital art by Richard Mapes . Food & Drinks: Food and drinks will be available for purchase from Catbird's kitchen and bars, including the rooftop tent bar. Parking: Free Street parking. Nearby paid parking lots have options around $6. Visit SpotHero to explore parking availability and current rates. Admission: Free, private event. Advance registration required.

events.title: Memory Cafe: Sing-Along with Swallow Hill Music
events.description: Memory Cafe is a fun place to socialize, relax, and engage with people experiencing memory loss and other cognitive changes along with their friends, families, and care partners. Each cafe has a focus—such as music or art—to facilitate the main goal, which is a social connection for individuals with shared experiences. At the Memory Cafe, you can just be yourself without worrying about remembering or forgetting. Theme: Sing-Along with Swallow Hill Music Description: Swallow Hill for an afternoon of singing and connection! We will sing through folk, pop, country, and rock ‘n roll classics to relax, uplift our spirit, and connect with one another through music. About Presenter: Singer-songwriter Jen Hitt will lead the group. Jen teaches Women of Folk and Fireside Folk at Swallow Hill Music, sings classically with St. Martin’s Chamber Choir and various churches and synagogues, and produces radio for Colorado Public Radio. This program is designed specifically for individuals with memory loss or dementia and their care partner or family members. Attendance by groups is not part of our program model. If you are a service provider and would like to bring 3 or more people, please email olderadults@denverlibrary.org at least 2 business days before the program and we will let you know if we are able accommodate your group.

events.title: Narcan/Naloxone & Overdose Response Training
events.description: This training will be facilitated by the Denver Department of Public Health and Environment (DDPHE) . Our overdose response training provides individuals with the basic understanding of opioids, how overdoses happen, as well as how to recognize and respond to an overdose. The training also orients attendees with some historic narrative of the overdose crisis, local data and resources, as well as other factors such as polysubstance use and illicit drug supply adulterants that affect drug user health. To request ASL, CART, or other disability related accommodations, contact programs@denverlibrary.org or call 720-865-1111 with a minimum five (5) business day notice.

events.title: Memory Cafe: Cookie Decoration
events.description: Memory Cafe is a fun place to socialize, relax, and engage with people experiencing memory loss and other cognitive changes along with their friends, families, and care partners. Each cafe has a focus—such as music or art—to facilitate the main goal, which is a social connection for individuals with shared experiences. At the Memory Cafe, you can just be yourself without worrying about remembering or forgetting. Theme: Cookie Decoration Description : Join us as we decorate delicious cookies and share memories about this delicious treat! This program is designed specifically for individuals with memory loss or dementia and their care partner or family members. Attendance by groups is not part of our program model. If you are a service provider and would like to bring 3 or more people, please email olderadults@denverlibrary.org at least 2 business days before the program and we will let you know if we are able accommodate your group.

events.title: Tour Central Library
events.description: Join us any Tuesday for a guided tour of the Central Library. Learn about its architecture and visit public places you may not find on your own. Have you ever wondered about the white "ribbon" on the grand staircase or the giant wooden sculpture on level 5? What about the fossils hidden in plain sight? Join the tour and find out all about it! Duration: Tour is approximately an hour and a half and includes constant walking, standing, and using the elevators or stairs. Group Size: Space is limited. Please plan to arrive early, tours start promptly at the given time and late arrivals cannot be accommodated. Where to Meet : Meet in the center of the main hall on level 1, by the couch circle (see photo). Parking: Please note that there is no free parking near Central. The Cultural Center Complex Garage provides hourly parking for a fee. If you require any mobility accommodations or would like to schedule a group tour for 5+ people, please request a tour using this form .
